AMD 收购 Taalas，通过在硅中蚀刻模型来提高推理性能

AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon

科技产品 作者 itvision 热度 931 回复 702 2026/08/07 04:23
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • In AMD’s latest bid to upset Nvidia's dominance in AI hardware, the House of Zen has acquired AI chip company Taalas, which bakes model weights directly into silicon in a process that promises to boost inference performance by an order of magnitude or more.The deal, announced at market close on Thursday, appears to be framed in much the same context as Nvidia’s $20 billion licensing deal with Groq last December: make high-performance “premium” inference services prized for AI agents, like code assistants, faster and cheaper to run. AMD didn’t disclose the terms of the deal, but from what we understand, this is an actual acquisition rather than an acquihire.Founded in 2023 and based in Toronto, Taalas’ approach to inference is radically different from conventional GPUs or the dataflow architectures that underpin Groq LPUs or Cerebras' waferscale accelerators.
  • REG AD

“足够好”的 LLM 功能（针对用例）将位于汽车、电器等的芯片上或芯片上。这将以电池级功耗提供 chatjimmy 的速度。

Probably this will also happen for software engineering. formerly_proven 2026/08/07 19:02
很明显，8B Taalas 芯片在台积电 N6 上已经达到了十字线大小。我的意思是，我们正在讨论的流程约为 100 MTr/mm²，ROM 每位大约需要一个晶体管，但可能可以比一般逻辑封装得更密集。比如说，150 兆位/平方毫米并不是很多。 N6 的十字线限制为 850 mm²。这大致跟踪，文章称该芯片有 8B 参数，并且显然在 ROM 上花费了大约一半的面积。 AI 加速器仅使用大量硅面积（每个 HBM3 芯片的硅面积 >1000mm²）是有原因的。我认为这不是非常可行，除非它们能够提高空间效率，例如使用 MLC ROM（如果尚未使用），或者使用具有 ROM 优化流程的堆叠芯片。然后我们又回到了不便宜的情况，尽管掩模版芯片一开始就不是便宜的区域。
It's quite telling that the 8B Taalas chip was already reticle-sized on TSMC N6. I mean, we're talking about a process that does ~100 MTr/mm², ROM needs about one transistor per bit, but can probably be packed more densely than general logic. Something like, say, 150 megabit/mm² is not a lot. N6 has a 850 mm² reticle limit. This roughly tracks, the article says the chip has 8B parameters and apparently spends about half the area on ROM. There's a reason AI accelerators just use a ton of silicon area (each HBM3 die is >1000mm² of silicon). I imagine this is not terribly viable unless they make it a lot more space efficient e.g. using MLC ROM if they don't already, or use stacked dies with a ROM-optimized process. And then we're back to not cheap, though reticle chips were never in the cheap area to begin with.

Tuna-Fish 2026/08/07 19:07
Taalas 利用低基数用一个晶体管存储一个 4 位权重。 （他们为 ROM 使用金属层走线，并连接一个存取晶体管来点亮 16 个选项之一。）

他们的系统对于权重来说确实非常高效，问题在于 KV 缓存。这就是为什么 HC1 只支持如此短的上下文，他们为此使用 SRAM，并为此花费了芯片剩余的大部分内容。最近提高注意力效率的进步可能对他们非常有用。

Taalas exploits the low cardinality to store one 4-bit weight with one transistor. (They are using metal layer traces for the ROM, and connecting an access transistor to light up one of 16 options.)

Their system is honestly very efficient for the weights, the problem is the KV-cache. That's why HC1 only supports such short context, they use SRAM for that and spend most of what's left of the die for it. The recent advancements that made attention more efficient are probably going to be very useful for them.

briansm 2026/08/08 13:31
Cerebras 拥有特殊技术来解决晶圆上的蚀刻错误/不良核心问题。这是可能的，因为它们的晶圆实际上是数百个相同的冗余核心副本。对于全球独一无二的模型来说，这是无法做到的。

在这种情况下蚀刻失败就像人类的脑损伤一样，各种奇怪的效果都会开始出现。

Cerebras have special techniques to work around etching errors / bad cores on their wafers. This is possible since their wafers are effectively hundreds of identical copies of redundant cores. Can't do that for a globally unique model.

Etching failure in that situation would be like brain-damage in a human, all sorts of weird effects would start appearing.
